resolutions.researcher_notes: Status 'operating' inferred from two independent inauguration reports: Petroleum Africa (Mubarak inaugurated the completed Upper Egypt line late Dec 2010 / early Jan 2011, final Sohag-Aswan phase commissioned Nov 2010) and al-Masry al-Youm (خط غاز الصعيد inaugurated by Mubarak in Aswan, Thu 30 Dec 2010). Both describe a completed, gas-carrying line -> operating. NOTE: the brief's current_ref (almasryalyoum details/103848) was flagged DEAD_LINK but resolves 200 today (false-negative); retained.

StartYear1=2009 supported by al-Masry al-Youm: the sixth/final phase (Girga-Aswan) 'الانتهاء منها في نوفمبر 2009' (completed Nov 2009). One strong Arabic source. CONTRADICTION/NUANCE to flag: the OFFICIAL inauguration was 30 Dec 2010 (al-Masry) and Petroleum Africa dates commissioning/inauguration to late 2010-Jan 2011; so 2009 = physical completion of the last stage, 2010 = ceremonial start-up. StartYear1=2009 is defensible as physical completion but the sheet may want 2010 for operational start.

Capacity=12.00 bcm/y supported by Petroleum Africa: 'With a current capacity of 8 bcm annually, capacity is expected to reach 12 bcm by 2014.' Single source. NUANCE to flag: 12 bcm is the DESIGN/target capacity (by 2014); throughput at inauguration was 8 bcm/y. al-Masry al-Youm gives no capacity figure; no second independent corroboration found for 12 bcm.

LengthKnown=930 km corroborated by two independent sources: al-Masry al-Youm ('الطول الإجمالي 930 كيلومتر') and Petroleum Africa ('The 930 km pipeline'). Minor discrepancy to note: Petroleum Africa's inauguration article and OGJ (2007) cite ~794-800 km, which are earlier partial-network figures before the full Dahshour-Aswan extension; 930 km is the completed full-network length.

Diameter values 32 and 30 in corroborated: Petroleum Africa gives per-segment diameters (Minya-Assiut 32 in; Assiut-Sohag 30 in; Sohag-Aswan 408 km 30 in) and OGJ gives 32 in for the Beni Suef/Abu Qorqas and Menya-Assiut phases; al-Masry al-Youm states diameters of '30 و32 بوصة'. CONTRADICTION to flag: the sheet's leading 36-inch value ('36, 32, 32, 32, 32, 30') is NOT supported by any source found — every source caps the multi-segment diameters at 32 in. The 30/32 values are solid; the 36 is unverified.

Route Dahshour (Giza) -> Aswan corroborated by two independent sources: al-Masry al-Youm (start دهشور, end أسوان) and Petroleum Africa (Cairo/Dahshour through Beni Suef, Minya, Assiut, Sohag to Aswan). StartLocation=Dahshour and EndLocation=Aswan both directly supported.

SegmentCost=9,300,000,000 USD literally matches Petroleum Africa: 'The 930 km pipeline was worth approximately $9.3 billion in investments.' STRONG CONTRADICTION to flag: two independent sources give a far lower cost in Egyptian pounds - al-Masry al-Youm 'حوالى 5.7 مليار جنيه' (~5.7 bn EGP) and Petroleum Africa's own inauguration article 'LE5.7 billion'. 5.7 bn EGP at 2010 rates is ~USD 1 bn, an order of magnitude below 9.3 bn. $9.3 bn for a 930 km gas line (~$10 M/km) is implausibly high and likely a units error (EGP mis-stated as USD) in the single source that matches the sheet. Value is technically sourced but low-confidence; recommend reviewing toward ~5.7 bn EGP.

Owner1=Egyptian Natural Gas Holding Co (EGAS, الشركة المصرية القابضة للغازات الطبيعية) named by al-Masry al-Youm among the participating entities (EGAS, South Valley Holding, Gasco, Petrojet, Enppi). Single source for EGAS specifically. NUANCE to flag: OGJ and the EIB project page (ref 20060137) name GASCO as executor/promoter, and Petroleum Africa names Nile Valley Gas Company (NVGC) as operator with Petrojet constructing - these are the operator/constructor roles, whereas EGAS is the state gas holding parent, so Owner1=EGAS 100% is reasonable as the owning state holding but is not independently confirmed at 100%.
